analysis.title: Weekly Economic Perspectives (November 6, 2026)
key_insights: US October nonfarm payrolls rose 165k versus a 59k Bloomberg consensus, and the unemployment rate eased to 4.1% from 4.2%. State Street reads this as reaffirming economic resilience despite oddities in the report.

State Street is skeptical of the reported services employment surge. Service-providing industries added 144k jobs, half in professional and business services, and the 19k rise in temporary help looks likely to reverse next month.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m but wage inflation moderated a tenth to 3.1% y/y. State Street calls wage inflation modest and consistent with a 2.0% inflation target.

The household survey showed participation up a tenth to 61.9%, the highest since March. Average unemployment duration jumped to 27.1 weeks and labor underutilization measures rose slightly, which State Street flags as puzzles that call for caution in reading the data.
US ISM Services was 54.5, little changed. The employment component rose to an eight-month high of 51.4, while business activity and new orders retreated but stayed at solid levels.
The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 25bps to 4.00% in an 8-1 vote. Catherine Mann dissented in favor of 50bps. The minutes and Monetary Policy Report were more hawkish than State Street expected.

The BoE expects inflation to rise to about 5% in Q2 2027, above the 4% threshold beyond which its research finds second-round effects more likely. Drivers are stronger growth, a steadier jobs market and a surge in oil and gas prices.
State Street expects BoE rates to peak at 4.25% by February, with risks skewed higher, and titles the piece 'December Hike In Play'.

The RBA hiked 25bp to 4.85%, its fifth hike this year, on a 6-3 vote, the highest cash rate since 2008. It dropped the September reference to potentially raising the cash rate further, but State Street views the overall message as hawkish at the margin.

The RBA raised its inflation forecasts. It sees trimmed mean inflation at 3.6% at end-2026 and 2.9% at end-2027, underlying inflation above 3% until late 2027, and upside inflation risks. Its unemployment forecast is about 4.9% by end-2027 and 5.1% by end-2028.

State Street is reluctant to call 4.85% the peak and sees scope for a 5-handle cash rate. Its base case is that the RBA is nearing the end of tightening, and it would be cautious about pushing materially beyond 5%.
Australian household spending rose 0.6% m/m in September and 6.8% y/y. Q3 volumes rose 0.7% q/q and 3.2% y/y, the strongest annual pace since early 2023. Discretionary spending was 6.9% higher y/y.
State Street expects Australian unemployment to rise toward 5.5% over the next 12 months, above the RBA's forecast path. It sees this as the main constraint on how far the RBA can tighten.

Other data in the week: US ISM Manufacturing was 55.5 versus 54.5 consensus, JOLTS openings were 7,523k versus 7,164k, Q3 nonfarm productivity was 3.6% versus 2.7%, and Michigan sentiment was 51.0 versus 48.0.
Canada's October unemployment rate rose to 6.7% from 6.5%, above expectations and the second consecutive monthly rise. German September retail sales fell 2.0% m/m versus a 0.4% consensus.

risk_factors: Oil and gas price surge adds to UK inflation pressure and could push the BoE beyond 4.25%.
Sticky inflation and resilient household demand could push the RBA cash rate into a 5-handle.
Australian labor market cooling more slowly than State Street expects would extend RBA tightening.
US payroll data show inconsistencies, including the services hiring surge and swings in participation, so the strength may reverse in coming months.
vol_and_positioning: The report says US election and AI jitters drove market volatility during the week while growth remained solid. It gives no vol levels.

tension_points.bull_case: The RBA dropped its explicit reference to further hikes and State Street's base case is that it is approaching the end of tightening. Unemployment rising toward 5.5% should eventually constrain how far it can go.
tension_points.bear_case: The RBA raised its inflation forecasts, sees upside inflation risks and trimmed mean inflation above 3% until late 2027. Resilient household spending could push the cash rate into a 5-handle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Household demand staying resilient, inflation proving sticky and the labor market cooling more slowly than State Street expects would take the cash rate into a 5-handle.

tension_points.bull_case: Payrolls of 165k beat the 59k consensus, unemployment fell to 4.1% and ISM Services employment hit an eight-month high.
tension_points.bear_case: The services hiring surge looks unconvincing, with temporary help likely to reverse. Unemployment duration rose to 27.1 weeks and underutilization measures rose slightly.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reversal of the 19k temporary help gain next month would undercut the strength implied by the October report.

theme_stances.key_argument: The RBA's raised inflation forecasts and inflation-expectations concern mean 4.85% should not be called the definitive peak.
theme_stances.evidence: we are reluctant to call 4.85% the definitive peak
